correctness.rationale: For N>D, the weights are strictly decreasing and violate hyponormality; diagonal weights are one. When N<D, MID implies complete monotonicity of h_n=-log(alpha_n^2) by differentiating the Hausdorff inequalities of gamma_n^s at s=0. The unique finite signed representing measure for h has masses c_k=(-1)^(k-1)(D^k-N^k)/k at distinct q^k; uniqueness of finite Borel measures on [0,1] forces every mass nonnegative. c_1>0 and c_2=(N^2-D^2)/2 then give N<0 and N<D<=-N; all later coefficients have the requisite signs. Conversely, nonnegative c_k give summable b_k=c_k/(1-q^k), and independent Poisson jumps with means s*b_k have the exact probability generating function needed for powered moment sequence gamma_n^s. Convergence follows from |N|,|D|<1 and q<1. All integer indices, real bases and positive Schur exponents are covered analytically; the supplied finite 1081-test checker is supplementary.

value.rationale: This is a natural *complete* classification for the geometrically regular unilateral shifts and resolves the explicit missing MID-exclusion part of the 2023 parameter-diagram conjecture, replacing the prior sufficient-region and numerical tests with a proof valid for every real p>1. The same calculation yields a uniquely specified finite-intensity compound-Poisson Berger measure for every positive Schur power, with an exact atom at 1 and even-intensity collapse on the sector boundary. This measures all powered moments, not merely demonstrating subnormality or re-labeling a known region. The signed Hausdorff atomic uniqueness step is structural, and the exact boundary answers an explicit motivated gap rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
